(3)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the equation
$5\cos^2 x=3(1+\sin x)$
can be written as
$5\sin^2 x+3\sin x-2=0$.
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence solve, for $0\leqslant x<360°$, the equation
$5\cos^2 x=3(1+\sin x)$,
giving your answers to 1 decimal place where appropriate.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $0=(5\sin x-2)(\sin x+1)$
A1 cso: $\sin x=\frac{2}{5}, -1$ (both)
B1: $\sin x=\frac{2}{5} \Rightarrow x=23.6$ ($\alpha=23.6$ or $156.4$)
M1: $x=156.4$ ($180-\alpha$)
B1: $\sin x=-1 \Rightarrow x=270$
(ignore extra solutions outside the range)

questions.stem:
$\mathrm{f}(x)=x^3-2x^2+ax+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
When $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is divided by $(x-2)$, the remainder is 1.
When $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is divided by $(x+1)$, the remainder is 28.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $\mathrm{f}(2)=1 \Rightarrow 8-2\times4+2a+b=1$
M1 A1: $\mathrm{f}(-1)=28 \Rightarrow -1-2-a+b=28$
M1 A1: solving $\begin{cases}2a+b=1\\-a+b=31\end{cases} \Rightarrow a=-10, b=21$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Show that $(x-3)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{f}(x)$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathrm{f}(3)=27-18+3a+b$
A1 c.s.o: $=27-18-30+21=0$ $\therefore (x-3)$ is a factor

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows the triangle $ABC$, with $AB=8$ cm, $AC=11$ cm and $\angle BAC=0.7$ radians. The arc $BD$, where $D$ lies on $AC$, is an arc of a circle with centre $A$ and radius 8 cm. The region $R$, shown shaded in Figure 1, is bounded by the straight lines $BC$ and $CD$ and the arc $BD$.
Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the length of the arc $BD$,
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the perimeter of $R$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures,
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $BC^2=8^2+11^2-2\times8\times11\times\cos0.7$
A1: $\Rightarrow BC=7.098$
M1, A1cao: $\Rightarrow$ Perimeter $=(a)+(11-8)+BC,=15.7$ (cm)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the area of $R$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1, A1: $\Delta=\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C=\frac{1}{2}\times11\times8\times\sin0.7,=$ AWRT $28.3$
M1, A1: Sector$=\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta=,\frac{1}{2}\times8^2\times0.7$
A1: Area of $R=28.345\ldots-22.4=5.9455=5.95$ (cm$^2$)

questions.stem: Figure 3 shows the plan of a stage in the shape of a rectangle joined to a semicircle. The length of the rectangular part is $2x$ metres and the width is $y$ metres. The diameter of the semicircular part is $2x$ metres. The perimeter of the stage is 80 m.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the area, $A$ m$^2$, of the stage is given by
$A=80x-\left(2+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)x^2$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Perimeter $\Rightarrow 2x+2y+\pi x=80$
B1: Area $\Rightarrow A=2xy+\frac{1}{2}\pi x^2$
M1: $y=\frac{80-2x-\pi x}{2}$ and sub in to $A$
$\Rightarrow A=80x-2x^2-\pi x^2+\frac{1}{2}\pi x^2$
A1 c.s.o: i.e. $A=80x-\left(2+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)x^2$*

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use calculus to find the value of $x$ at which $A$ has a stationary value.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1, A1: $\frac{dA}{dx}=80-2\left(2+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)x$ or $80-4x-\pi x$ (or equiv.)
M1, A1: $\frac{dA}{dx}=0 \Rightarrow 40=\left(2+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)x$ so $x=\frac{40}{2+\frac{\pi}{2}}$ or $\frac{80}{4+\pi}$ or awrt $11.2$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Prove that the value of $x$ you found in part (b) gives the maximum value of $A$.
(2)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Calculate, to the nearest m$^2$, the maximum area of the stage.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Max Area $=80(b)-\left(2+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)(b)^2$
A1 cao: $=448$ (m$^2$) (448 only for A1)
